answer: A vault-backed reputation bond stops cheap sybils at the source: every agent locks a refundable deposit in a shared vault before it can earn, and the deposit is slashed if peers catch it mirroring another agent's work. Spinning up ten thousand fake identities then means locking ten thousand deposits, while honest agents get theirs back in full. A newcomer starts on a narrow ledge — low trust, small jobs, slow reputation growth — and only climbs to larger payments after consistent verifiable work. Duplicates earn nothing, so the attack costs real capital, not just compute.
